standard_prerequisites.name: For a Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres the number of branches of the ring and of its completion agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Feeds the branch count into the criterion comparing branches with the completion, which is what produces the uniqueness of the minimal prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: If the number of branches of a local ring and its completion agree, then the completion of the henselization modulo a minimal prime has a unique minimal prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the formal catenarity of the henselization by definition of that notion.

standard_prerequisites.name: A formally catenary Noetherian local ring is universally catenary, and a unibranch ring has henselization with a unique minimal prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns formal catenarity into universal catenarity in the first case, and supplies the uniqueness of the minimal prime that starts the second case.

core_obligations: Use the statement on the number of branches for geometrically normal formal fibres to see that the ring and its completion have the same number of branches, and apply the criterion comparing branches with the completion to conclude that for every minimal prime of the henselization the completion modulo the image of that prime has a unique minimal prime (proof lines 32511-32517).

Conclude that the henselization is formally catenary by definition of formal catenarity and hence universally catenary by the Ratliff criterion, which gives the first conclusion (proof lines 32517-32519).

For the second conclusion, assume the ring is unibranch and use the characterization of unibranchness through the henselization having a unique minimal prime to see that the completion has a unique minimal prime as well (proof lines 32519-32522).
Conclude in the same way that the ring is formally catenary and therefore universally catenary (proof lines 32522-32523).
proof_roadmap: Compare branch numbers through the geometrically normal hypothesis and derive the unique minimal prime of the completion of the henselization modulo a minimal prime (proof lines 32511-32517).
Read off formal catenarity and universal catenarity of the henselization (proof lines 32517-32519).
In the unibranch case, transfer uniqueness of the minimal prime to the completion and conclude in the same way (proof lines 32519-32522).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that a Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres has universally catenary henselization, and that the ring itself is universally catenary when it is unibranch (statement lines 32497-32509). The proof is a two-step transfer of branch counts: the geometrically normal hypothesis makes the number of branches of the ring and of its completion agree, the branch-count criterion then gives the uniqueness of the minimal prime of the completion of the henselization modulo any of its minimal primes, which is precisely formal catenarity and hence universal catenarity by the Ratliff criterion; in the unibranch case the uniqueness of the minimal prime is transferred to the ring itself and the same criterion is applied again (proof lines 32511-32523). The transfer of the branch count through the henselization is the device that makes both assertions follow from one computation. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed; the three same-chapter references are carried as navigation stubs.
